current.text: Yahoo lists him as questionable with an ankle injury.
Tiago Splitter is the new Bulls head coach. Billy Donovan, who pulled him early after mistakes, is gone.
Splitter is expected to give him more ball handling and point forward duties. How much Splitter will empower him is still an open question.
He is in the projected starting five with Josh Giddey, Norman Powell, Caleb Wilson and Nick Claxton. On a big-focused roster he plays small forward, out of position.
Nikola Vucevic and Coby White have left Chicago, which frees usage. Norman Powell and Caleb Wilson have arrived.

Most experts expect his usage and shot volume to rise as the first or second option, possibly second on the team ahead of Giddey and Wilson. They expect it to land below his late-season 25% but above his season-long 22%. One expert disagrees and expects Powell to lead the team in usage, with Buzelis lower.
Experts see no playing-time worry and expect about 32 minutes a game.
Experts expect a big third-year breakout.
His blocks may drop next to Caleb Wilson and at small forward, even with more minutes. His assists should go up.
Experts rank him as a top-50 player in 9-cat, finishing around 50. They say his Yahoo rank is still too low even after it rose to 64.
Draft advice: do not take him around pick 40. The 60s are a good spot, and the late 40s and 50s are acceptable to experts who want him.
His auction price should be about 20 USD. He went for 22 USD in an expert mock auction, and Josh, a big fan, would only pay value.
Experts project Chicago as a bad team, probably bottom ten, with about 32 wins.
The Bulls played very fast late last season and are expected to play an up-tempo transition style.
Chicago has 15 back-to-backs, one below the maximum. Its fantasy playoff schedule is 3-3-4 games (10) with our March 28 end.

durable.text: Blocks are his standout category. He blocks shots at a league-outlier rate, especially for a forward.
He makes many threes for a forward, but at a modest percentage (about 35% last season).
In a big-minutes role he produces both blocks and threes.
He has missed few games in his first two seasons.

note: The experts see him as a top-50 9-cat player who costs about 20 USD. He fits any build because no category is flagged weak, and his blocks and threes from the forward spot are the main draw. Yahoo (average cost 6 USD, value 16 USD) and ESPN (7 USD) price him low, but he went for 12 USD in our league last year and for 22 USD in an expert mock auction, so expect to pay about 15 to 22 USD. Early in the season, check his Q ankle status, whether Splitter gives him about 32 minutes and the usage the experts expect, and whether his blocks hold next to Caleb Wilson and Claxton.
